title: Skill discovery runs on a 60-char description and nobody owns a skill: 212 stale, 72 archived, usage telemetry never consulted at selection
reasoning: Borrowed from rlaope/oh-my-hermes src/skills/catalog.py, which ships 418 indexed skills with categories and triggers; the mechanism is worth copying, the library is not. Skills are the cheapest capability amplification the fleet has and they are currently undiscoverable: discovery is the description prefix, and 71% of ours fail it. Measured 2026-10-28 across ~/coding-hermes-skills (42 SKILL.md, 12 trigger-compliant, 3 empty, 6 over length) and ~/.hermes/skills (315 skills, 81 compliant, 94 over length, 11 with triggers[], 13 with tags, 0 with owner). Without a catalog nobody can answer which skills are used, which are dead, or which project owns each one. Evidence: .hermes/hermes-agent/scripts/build_skills_index.py, .hermes/hermes-agent/tools/skill_usage.py, ~/.hermes/skills/.usage.json (1,790 entries), curator enabled in config.yaml:661. The catalog existed; the selection surface and ownership did not.
acceptance_criteria: CORRECTED PREMISE (2026-10-28): a catalog and usage telemetry already exist and I filed this row as if they did not. scripts/build_skills_index.py builds an index, ~/.hermes/skills/.usage.json holds 1,790 entries with use_count, view_count, patch_count, state (active/stale/archived) and pinned, and curator is enabled (interval 168h, stale_after 30d) - it covers 267 of 315 installed skills and 38 of 42 fleet-repo skills. The real gaps are four. (1) Ownership: no skill declares an owner and 4 fleet-repo skills are untracked entirely. (2) Selection: the agent picks a skill from its description alone, never from usage or state, so 212 stale skills stay equally weighted against proven ones and 'never used' is never surfaced at the moment of choice. (3) Standards: only 81 of 315 installed descriptions open with a trigger sentence and 94 exceed the front-load budget; the repo mirrors it at 12 of 42. (4) Retirement: 72 archived and 0 pinned means nothing is deliberately protected or pruned. Deliver an owner field with a backfill; a task-vocabulary lookup ('skills find <task>') that ranks candidates by usage state and restricts to the project's scope; trigger-shaped descriptions enforced by the authoring guard in both roots; and a monthly never-used report that proposes merge or archive per skill.
acceptance: Every skill (315 installed + 42 repo) has an owner or is listed unattributable; a task-vocabulary lookup returns ranked candidates for 10 real fleet tasks; description compliance reaches 95% in both roots; a never-used report exists naming each skill with a proposed action.
